blocks.title: What paint correction is, and what it takes out of your paint.
body: Paint correction is **machine polishing**. Your color sits under a layer of clear coat, and that clear coat is where swirl marks, light scratches, oxidation and water spots live. We polish it by machine until the marks are out and the paint reflects cleanly again.

Wax sits on top of the paint and washes off in weeks, and the marks under it are still there when it does. Correction does not cover anything up. The marks are **polished out of the clear coat**. Here is what it removes:
checks: **Swirl marks.** The fine, circular scratches you see in direct sun. Brush-style automatic washes put them into any finish.
**Light scratches.** Marks that sit in the clear coat and have not gone through it.
**Oxidation.** The dull, faded look that builds up on paint left unprotected.
**Water spots.** The marks left behind where water dried on the panel.
**Dullness.** With the marks gone, the gloss comes back. The shine in our after photos comes from correcting the paint first.

blocks.title: What correction fixes, and what it cannot.
blocks.intro: Polishing works on the clear coat that is there. It is not repainting. Here is where the line sits, so you know what to expect before you book.

items.title: Swirl marks and wash marks
items.body: The fine scratches that years of washing leave behind, easiest to see on dark paint in direct sun. They sit in the clear coat, which is the layer a machine polish works on.

items.title: Rock chips
items.body: A chip is a spot where the paint is gone. Polishing cannot put paint back, so a chip will still be there after correction.

items.title: Light scratches
items.body: Scratches that are in the clear coat and have not gone through it. A one-step polish removes roughly 60 to 70% of light swirls and scratches. A multi-stage correction goes further.

items.title: Scratches through the clear coat
items.body: A scratch that has cut through the clear coat is deeper than polishing reaches. We point these out when we inspect the paint, before any work starts.

items.title: Oxidation and water spots
items.body: Dull, faded paint and the marks water leaves when it dries on a panel. The 2021 Chevy Silverado 2500HD in our photos came in with heavy oxidation and water spots. Both polished out.

items.title: Failed clear coat
items.body: When the clear coat itself has failed, there is nothing sound left to polish. **Correction is not repainting**, and we will say so plainly if that is what we find on your vehicle.

blocks.title: Five steps from dull paint to corrected and protected.
blocks.intro: The polisher is only one part of the job. Here is what your vehicle goes through at our shop, in order.

steps.title: Inspection under shop lighting
steps.body: We look over your paint under shop lighting and note the swirls, scratches and any existing damage. You hear which marks will polish out and which will not before we touch the car.

steps.title: Wash and decontamination
steps.body: A full decontamination wash: iron and tar removal, then a clay treatment to pull out the embedded grit a normal wash leaves behind. Paint has to be clean before a polisher touches it.

steps.title: Machine polish
steps.body: Swirls, light scratches and oxidation are machine polished out of the clear coat. Light defects get a one-step polish. Heavier paint gets a multi-stage correction, and Matt, our lead technician, handles the heaviest of it.

steps.title: Panel wipe
steps.body: Every panel is wiped down to strip the polishing oils, so whatever goes on next bonds to clean clear coat and not to residue.

steps.title: Protection
steps.body: Corrected paint gets protected before it leaves. Polish & Protect is sealed for 6 months, and the Luxury Refresh gets a sealant too. With a ceramic coating package, this is where the coating goes on.

blocks.footnote: Paint correction is done at the shop only. If you cannot get the vehicle to us, ask about our [pick-up and drop-off valet service](/mobile-detailing/): we collect it, do the work at the shop and bring it back.

faq.q: What is the difference between a one-step polish and a multi-stage correction?
faq.a:
A one-step polish is a single polishing stage. It removes roughly 60 to 70% of light swirls and scratches and brings the gloss back. It is what you get in Polish & Protect and in the Luxury Refresh.

A multi-stage correction, which you may hear us call a 2 step, is for heavier defects: heavy swirls, oxidation and paint that one stage will not clear. It takes more time, so it is quoted per vehicle after we see the paint. We will tell you which one your paint needs, and we will not sell you the longer job if the shorter one will do it.

faq.q: How long does paint correction take?
faq.a:
Polish & Protect takes about 4.5 to 5 hours. The Luxury Refresh, which includes a full interior detail too, takes about 7 hours. Larger vehicles take longer.

A multi-stage correction takes longer again, and how much longer depends on the paint. We give you a time window when we quote your vehicle. If you would rather not arrange a ride, our pick-up and drop-off valet collects the vehicle and brings it back when the work is done.

faq.q: Will paint correction remove every scratch?
faq.a:
No, and we would rather say so now than at pickup. A one-step polish removes roughly 60 to 70% of light swirls and scratches. A multi-stage correction takes out more.

Some damage is outside what polishing can do: rock chips, scratches that have gone through the clear coat, and clear coat that has failed. Correction is not repainting. We look over the paint under shop lighting before any work starts and tell you which marks will come out and which will stay.

faq.q: Do I need a ceramic coating after paint correction?
faq.a:
You do not need one. Polish & Protect is sealed for 6 months, and the Luxury Refresh includes a sealant on the paint too.

A coating is for when you want the corrected finish protected for years and not months. Our [ceramic coating packages](/ceramic-coating/) run 1, 3 and 5 years, and paint correction is already included in every one, done right before the coating goes on. If you know you want a coating, book the coating and the correction comes with it.

faq.q: Can you do paint correction at my home?
faq.a:
No. Paint correction is done at our shop only. Machine polishing needs enclosed bays and controlled lighting, and a driveway gives us wind, dust and weather to work against.

If getting to Clinton Township is the obstacle, use our pick-up and drop-off valet. We collect the vehicle from your home or workplace, correct it at the shop and bring it back. Mobile detailing is still available for interior details and Wash & Seal, which do not need the shop.

faq.q: How much does paint correction cost?
faq.a:
A one-step polish has set starting prices. Polish & Protect, an exterior package, is from $344.99. The Luxury Refresh, a full interior and exterior detail with a one-step polish, is from $439.99. Both are for a coupe or sedan in average condition, and SUVs and trucks are quoted for their size.

A multi-stage correction is quoted per vehicle after we see the paint. Text us photos or use the quote form on this page and we will give you a real number. Financing is available through Affirm and Klarna.

faq.q: How do I keep swirl marks from coming back?
faq.a:
Mostly by changing how the car gets washed. Brush-style automatic washes put swirls into any finish, corrected or not, and wiping dust off dry paint drags grit across the clear coat. Touchless washes are fine, and so is a gentle hand wash.

A ceramic coating helps as well. Grime does not grip a coated surface, so a rinse and a gentle wash does the job.
